query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: comparative_positioning
per_column.rationale: Comparative positioning captures how a product stacks up against alternatives (superior/inferior/best-in-category). This is a relational judgment ABOUT the product relative to others, not a constitutive aspect OF food quality itself. Intrinsic facets of food quality would be things like taste/flavor, texture, freshness, aroma, or ingredient quality. Being 'better than homemade' is an evaluative comparison that may correlate with quality but does not decompose the concept into its parts.

judge.rationale: The single added column is a comparative/relational assessment rather than a meronymic part of food quality. It does not carve food_quality into non-overlapping intrinsic aspects (taste, texture, freshness, etc.), so there is no facet set to evaluate. With no constitutive facets present, both mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness are 0.
